full_judgment:
2. The petitioners being plaintiffs instituted a suit for declaration of title in the schedule property before the Court of Munsif, Sadar Upazila, Faridpur, for correction of record of right. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that 52 decimals of land of SA plot No. 58, SA Khatian No. 164 under Mouza No. 54 Pearpur at Alphadangha, PS, under the district of Faridpur along with other properties totaling an area of 4.41 acres of land belonged to Huzzatullah Sarder by way of patta obtained from Zaminder Bhubhon Mohon. The suit land originally belonged to CS Khatian No. 317 CS plot No. 173 of Mouza Astail, an area of 3.27 acres of land owned by Huzzatullah Sarder by taking patta from the aforesaid Zaminder and the suit land situated on the north side of aforesaid CS plot No. 173 as poyosti land, which was recorded in Pearpur mouza under SA Khatian No. 164 in plot No. 58. Huzzatullah died leaving behind 8 sons and one daughter and Huzzatullah's son Elem Sarder also died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 1-8, but one Nurul Huq Sarder with a malafide intention during SA operation recorded the suit land in the name of defendant Nos. 1-2 which was disclosed by one son of Nurul Huq Sarder in the month of Chaitra, 1988 Bengali year, hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant No. 2 now opposite party No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint. The defendants' case, in short, is that the north side of Astail Mouza under CS Khatian No. 173 was the Modhumoti river, and the land of Khatian No. 173 had originally belonged to Huzzatullah Sarder who left 8 sons as his successors and one of the sons Elem Sarder, the father of the plaintiffs, settled the land of CS Khatian No. 173 by registered deed on 17th Magh, 1358 BS to one Altu Sarder and Nurul Huq Sarder and the land was on the north side of CS Khatian No. 173 as Poyosti of Madhumoti River and Nurul Huq Sarder possessed 90 decimals of land from which he transferred 58 decimals of land (out of said 90 decimals) to the defendant No. 2 and the defendant has been possessing the suit land. 

 11. The trial Court also found that the defendant No. 2 did not produce any documents to prove that the predecessor in interest of the defendants has transferred 0.58 acres land to the wife of Nurul Huq Sarder. It is further observed that there was no reason why Nurul Huq Sarder has given 58 decimals of land to defendant No. 2. It is further observed by the trial Court that plaintiffs have exhibited SA Khatian No. 164 as Exhibit 2 from where it is evident that defendant No. 2 was the owner of one anna land. In this case defendant No. 1 has appeared before the Court as plaintiff's witness No. 5 and stated that he had settled the matter with the plaintiff amicably. SA recorded owners Wahed Sarder son of Huzzatullah and son of Habibur Rahman have deposed before the Court in favour of the plaintiffs. It is further evident from the judgment of the trial Court that DW 5 Bashu Deb has stated that he has measured the land in question and possession has been given in favour of the plaintiff. He has further stated that the suit land was possessed by Elem and now the plaintiff No. 1 has been possessing the land but the appellate Court in his judgment has observed that the plaintiff could not prove its case beyond reasonable doubt without giving any reasonable cause in support of such observation. Though the defendant has claimed that the land was given patta to defendant No. 2 by Nurul Huq but no document in support of this statement has been produced before the Court. Moreover, the defendant could not produce any document in support of the owner ship of 0.58 acres of land by Nurul Huq Sarder. It is evident that the plaintiffs have exhibited documents and produced witness before the Court which is considered by the trial Court but the Court of appeal has not considered those. The appellate Court being the last Court of facts without considering material facts and circumstances as well as oral and documentary evidence has set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in an unlawful manner. Moreover, at the time of hearing the learned Advocate for the opposite party could not point out any error, illegality or conformity of law in the judgment passed by the trial Court.
